# Consent sign-in

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Identity provider · **Label:** `feature:consent-auth` · **Epic:** [#127](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/127) · **Tickets:** 7 (2S 5M)

Employees sign in to a consent portal on the CP with their IdP identity through a dedicated `warden-portal` OIDC client. The portal session is a separate type from the admin console and has no console privileges. When `consent.idpLink.enabled` is on, the login requests offline_access, and the CP stores the user's refresh token in the CP-only user credential store (`consent.store`), which no worker can read. P3 offboarding later uses that token to detect disabled users. Nothing in this feature exists in code yet. It builds on the P1 cpstate store, OIDC login flow, sessions, block list and ID-token verifier, and stays off unless a `consent:` block in the operator's --config enables it.

## How we build it

- Scope: CP only. No worker or hot-path change. Routes are mounted only when the CP-local `consent:` block in the operator-owned --config has `enabled: true`. The block is `json:"-"` on config.Policy, never on policyWire or SettingsWire, and read by a new resolveConsent in cmd/proxy, modeled on resolveConsole (W-P1-SSO-02). The dashboard writers WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteIntegrations and WriteDetection keep it byte-identical. Enabling it requires console.auth=oidc and --state-dir, or the CP refuses to start: an open console could edit the policy, scope caps and secret mappings that the portal trusts.
- Config (new): `consent.enabled` (default false); `consent.oidc {issuer, clientID (default warden-portal), clientSecretEnv, redirectURL (<cp-browser-url>/portal/callback), allowInsecureIssuer}`. Scopes are fixed: openid email profile groups, plus offline_access when idpLink is enabled. `consent.allowedGroups` is optional; empty means any user of the issuer. `consent.session {idle: 30m, absolute: 8h}` uses the same key names as console.session; the defaults are shorter than the console's 1h/12h because a portal session can approve third-party access for agents. `consent.idpLink {enabled: true, refreshLifetime: 720h}`, where 720h matches Dex absoluteLifetime from W-P1-DEX-01. Validation: 0 < idle <= absolute <= 24h; https issuer and redirectURL unless loopback or allowInsecureIssuer; the redirectURL path is exactly /portal/callback; an empty secret env fails startup naming the variable, never its value. Consent always requires console.auth=oidc and a real OIDC issuer: there is no --dev or demo path that runs consent or the IdP link without it, so dev and demo setups use the p1-dex stack (W-P1-DEX-02).
- Issuer binding: consent.oidc.issuer must equal the identity.issuer that workers verify against (W-P1-VRFY-01). Otherwise a portal sub would never match a data-plane sub. The CP checks this at startup, and the CP settings writer rejects an identity.issuer change that breaks it (400 identity_issuer_mismatch). The identity key is (iss, sub); email is for display only.
- Dex client: add static client `warden-portal` (confidential, secretEnv WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, redirect https://localhost:7070/portal/callback, grant types authorization_code and refresh_token) to deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml and config.dev.yaml. It is kept out of `warden`'s trustedPeers, so the CP-held refresh token can never mint aud=warden data-plane tokens. Warden code makes no Dex-specific calls.
- Shared web auth: P1 puts the OIDC flow and session code inside internal/controlplane, and internal/portal and internal/oauthbroker cannot import it, because controlplane mounts both. A refactor with no behaviour change moves it into a new package internal/webauth: a lazy provider with backoff, the oidc_pending store with a new `purpose` column (console|portal), a SessionStore parameterized by table, cookie name and CSRF label, the code exchange plus identity.NewIDTokenVerifier, and an httptest fake OIDC provider in internal/webauth/webauthtest.
- Login flow: GET /portal/login and GET /portal/callback use auth code with S256 PKCE, state and nonce. The pending row has purpose=portal, a 10m TTL, a single-use atomic consume and the 10k cap, and is bound to the browser by the `__Host-warden_portal_login` cookie, separate from the console's `__Host-warden_login`. A console state fails on /portal/callback and the reverse. The ID token is verified with identity.NewIDTokenVerifier (Audience=consent clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], nonce, RS256/ES256, 60s skew). `next` accepts only same-origin paths under /portal/ or /connect/; anything else goes to /portal.
- Admission: the callback creates no session and writes nothing when the principal's sub or email is on the P1 block list (login_error=blocked), when allowedGroups is set and no group matches (not_allowed), or when idpLink is enabled and the token response has no refresh_token (502, offline_access_not_granted).
- Portal sessions: cpstate migration `portal_sessions/0001` adds portal_sessions(id_hash, iss, sub, email, groups_json, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at), built with webauth.SessionStore. The id is 32 random bytes and only its sha256 is stored. last_seen_at is written at most once a minute, expiry uses the CP clock, and sessions survive restarts. The cookie is `__Host-warden_portal` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https. `warden_portal` is used only for http loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, with a startup warning.
- Isolation: the console middleware reads only the console cookie and the `sessions` table. The portal middleware reads only the portal cookie and `portal_sessions`. portal.Principal is its own type in its own context key, so no console authz check can ever see it. The portal middleware ignores console cookies, WARDEN_CP_TOKEN, worker tokens and wak_ API keys, and rechecks the block list on each request from the in-memory BlockStore snapshot. Exported portal.RequireSession and portal.PrincipalFrom serve /portal/* and /connect/* (W-P3-BRKR-03).
- CSRF: every non-GET request behind RequireSession needs `X-Warden-CSRF`, or a `csrf` form field on urlencoded posts. The value is HMAC-SHA256(raw portal session id, "warden-portal-csrf"), so a console token (label "warden-csrf") never validates on the portal. Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin. GET /portal/api/me serves the token. POST /portal/logout deletes the session row and clears the cookie, but leaves the IdP link.
- IdP link storage: the refresh token is written to the CP-only user credential store `consent.store` (W-P3-CSIG-06) at logical key `secrets.IdPLinkKey(userKey)` = `idp/<userKey>`, where userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub): the lowercase hex of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256("warden-user-v1\x00" + iss + "\x00" + sub), 32 characters. Every P3 feature builds per-user keys only through these W-P3-CSIG-06 helpers. With the default namePrefix the backend name is `warden-cp/idp/<userKey>`. No worker ever gets a credential for consent.store, and the CP refuses to start when it overlaps the secretStore whose credential the CP sends to workers. Migration `idp_links/0001` adds idp_links(iss, sub, user_key, email, secret_key, refresh_ref, generation, linked_at, refresh_issued_at, relink_due_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status, offboarded_at). It has no value-bearing column; refresh_ref = secrets.Ref(token).String().
- Write ordering and concurrency: writes are serialized per user_key with an in-process keyed mutex. Login does the secret Put first, then an upsert that increments generation. LinkStore.Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, expectedGeneration, token) takes the same mutex, returns ErrStaleGeneration without writing when the stored generation differs, and otherwise does the Put and then UPDATE ... WHERE generation=? (incrementing it), so the W-P3-OFFB-02 job never overwrites a newer login. relink_due_at = refresh_issued_at + idpLink.refreshLifetime lets offboarding tell Dex absolute expiry apart from a disabled user. A failed Put returns 503 secret_store_unavailable with no session and no row (fail-closed).
- Store and guards (W-P3-CSIG-06): the CP-local `consent.store` block {backend aws|vault|echo, namePrefix (default `warden-cp/`), aws{region}, vault{addr, mount, namespace, tokenEnv}} is the one CP-only store for every per-user credential in P3: `idp/<userKey>` (this feature), `users/<userKey>/<provider>` and `revoking/<userKey>/<provider>` (p3-oauth-broker, p3-consent-portal) and `oauth-clients/<provider>` client secrets. Credentials come only from the CP environment or role, never from YAML or the wire; vault is accepted once W-P3-PUS-01 lands, and echo only with --dev. Today the CP sends its secretStore credential to workers over SettingsWire.Secrets, so the CP refuses to start when consent.store resolves to the same backend with an overlapping prefix. New optional interface secrets.Persistent { Persists() bool }, false for EchoStore and true for awsSecretStore (and later Vault KV v2); with idpLink enabled the store must be persistent. Reserved logical prefixes `idp/`, `users/`, `revoking/` and `oauth-clients/` (secrets.IsReservedKey): config validation rejects static SecretMapping placeholders that use them, storeFetcher.Fetch refuses them, and /central/secrets returns 403 reserved_key on PUT and DELETE and leaves them out of List, so no policy or console edit can make a worker swap in, read or overwrite a per-user credential.
- Revocation: PortalSessionStore.DeleteBySub and DeleteByEmail are called from the W-P1-BLOCK-07 BlockStore.Add path, so blocking or offboarding ends portal sessions at once. GET and DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?kind=portal (admin only) extend W-P1-SSO-08. Expired sessions and pending rows are swept every minute.
- Degraded modes: discovery is lazy, as in P1. With the IdP down, only /portal/login and /portal/callback return 503 idp_unavailable; existing portal sessions keep working, and CP start and /policy are unaffected. With consent.store down, new logins fail with 503 while existing sessions keep working. A minimal GET /portal stub (signed-in email, link status, relink_due_at, logout) is served until W-P3-PORT-01 replaces it.
- Observability: log records portal_login{result,reason}, portal_logout, portal_session_revoked and idp_link_stored (secret Reference and generation only), plus W-P1-AAUD-02 Recorder entries for portal login, logout and `user.idp_linked`. In-memory counters: portal logins by result, active portal sessions, and IdP link writes by result. The code, verifier, nonce, ID token, refresh token, cookie and CSRF value are never logged.

## Done when

Setup: a CP running with console.auth=oidc, `consent.enabled: true` in --config, an existing --state-dir and a persistent secret store, against the reference Dex stack that has the warden-portal client. A seeded LDAP user signs in through /portal/login and lands on /portal with a __Host-warden_portal session. consent.store holds `idp/<secrets.UserKey(iss,sub)>`, and idp_links holds only (iss, sub), a Reference, the generation and the dates. The same portal cookie gets 401 on every /dashboard/api/* route and on /central/secrets. A portal POST without a matching X-Warden-CSRF header, or with a foreign Origin, gets 403. A blocked user cannot sign in, and blocking a signed-in user ends their portal session. The CP refuses to start with an echo consent.store while idpLink is enabled, with a consent.store that overlaps the distributed secretStore, or with a placeholder under a reserved prefix, and a login without a refresh token creates no session. With Dex stopped, /portal/login returns 503 while existing portal sessions and worker /policy keep working. An ID token issued to warden-portal is rejected by the worker verifier, and no log line contains the code, verifier, nonce, ID token, refresh token or cookie value.

### 1/7 · W-P3-CSIG-01

**Add the CP-local consent config block and the warden-portal Dex client**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#128](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/128)

Add the operator-owned `consent:` block, modeled on the P1 console block: read only from --config, `json:"-"`, never on the wire, and kept byte-identical by the dashboard writers. Add the `warden-portal` static client to the reference Dex configs (carried forward from p1-dex). The session keys match the console (`idle`, `absolute`) but have shorter defaults, because the portal can approve third-party access. The OIDC client and routes are built later, in W-P3-CSIG-02; with no block, or with `enabled: false`, nothing changes.

**Requirements**

- internal/config/consent.go (new): ConsentConfig{Enabled bool; OIDC ConsentOIDC; AllowedGroups []string; Session ConsentSession; IdPLink ConsentIdPLink}, ConsentOIDC{Issuer, ClientID, ClientSecretEnv, RedirectURL string; AllowInsecureIssuer bool}, ConsentSession{Idle, Absolute time.Duration}, ConsentIdPLink{Enabled bool; RefreshLifetime time.Duration}. Defaults: clientID warden-portal, idle 30m, absolute 8h, idpLink.enabled true, refreshLifetime 720h. The struct comment records why the session defaults are shorter than the console's. The struct leaves room for later `store` (W-P3-CSIG-06), `providers` and `connect` (W-P3-BRKR-01), `publicURL` (W-P3-JIT-01) and `offboarding` (W-P3-OFFB-02) keys.
- Strict parsing: unknown keys are rejected. Validation when enabled: issuer, clientSecretEnv and redirectURL are required; issuer and redirectURL are https unless the host is loopback or allowInsecureIssuer is true (warning); the redirectURL is absolute, its path is exactly /portal/callback, and it differs from console.oidc.redirectURL; 0 < idle <= absolute <= 24h; refreshLifetime > 0.
- Policy.Consent has `json:"-"`; rawConfig accepts `consent:` under KnownFields(true), so workers and the served copy still parse. New config.LoadConsent(path) reads only the consent node. cmd/proxy calls it on --config, never the served path; a different block in <state-dir>/config.yaml is ignored with a warning.
- Startup checks in resolveConsent when enabled: console.auth must be oidc, with no --dev or demo bypass (dev setups use the W-P1-DEX-02 Dex stack), and idpLink cannot be skipped by a dev flag; --state-dir is required; os.Getenv(clientSecretEnv) must be non-empty (the error names the variable, never the value); consent.oidc.issuer must equal the identity.issuer in the loaded policy (W-P1-VRFY-01). The CP settings writer rejects a later identity.issuer change that breaks this with 400 identity_issuer_mismatch.
- Dex: add `warden-portal` (confidential, secretEnv WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET, redirectURIs [https://localhost:7070/portal/callback]) to deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml and config.dev.yaml. It is not added to `warden`'s trustedPeers. Add `${WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET:?}` to deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml and a placeholder to deploy/compose/dex/.env.example.
- Back-compat: with no consent block, behaviour and existing tests are unchanged and no /portal route is mounted.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/config/consent.go (new) with the types, defaults, validateConsent (same https/loopback helper as validateConsole) and LoadConsent(path), reusing the strict decoder that LoadConsole uses.
2. In internal/config/config.go add an unexported rawConsent and `Consent *rawConsent `yaml:"consent"`` to rawConfig, convert it into Policy.Consent next to Console, and call validateConsent from validate().
3. In cmd/proxy/controlplane.go add resolveConsent(opts, servedPath, pol) (new), mirroring resolveConsole: load from opts.configPath, warn on a differing served block, run the startup checks, and pass the result in a new controlplane.Config.Consent *config.ConsentConfig field (nil when disabled).
4. In the CP settings writer in internal/controlplane/controlplane.go, reject an identity.issuer that differs from Config.Consent.OIDC.Issuer while consent is enabled.
5. Add the warden-portal client to deploy/compose/dex/config.yaml and config.dev.yaml, and the env var to docker-compose.identity.yml and dex/.env.example. Explain the client and why it is not a trusted peer in deploy/compose/dex/README.md.
6. Extend TestDexReferenceConfig in test/deploy/dex_config_test.go (from W-P1-DEX-01): the client set includes warden-portal with its redirect and no `secret` field, and `warden`.trustedPeers does not contain warden-portal. Confirm that scripts/check-secrets.sh covers the new client.
7. Add a commented consent example to configs/config.control-plane.yaml matching the compose client (issuer http://dex:5556/dex, allowInsecureIssuer true).
8. Tests: internal/config/consent_test.go (new); TestConsentNotOnWire and TestWritersPreserveConsentBlock in internal/controlplane; TestResolveConsent in cmd/proxy/commands_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Table tests cover a valid block, missing issuer, missing clientSecretEnv, an http non-loopback issuer without allowInsecureIssuer, a redirectURL path other than /portal/callback, a redirectURL equal to the console one, and idle > absolute or absolute > 24h: `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsentConfig`

### 2/7 · W-P3-CSIG-02

**Implement portal login, callback and session store**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#129](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/129)

Add the new internal/portal package with GET /portal/login, GET /portal/callback and the portal_sessions store, built on the shared internal/webauth code from W-P3-CSIG-05. Login uses the warden-portal client, a purpose=portal pending row and its own browser-binding cookie. Blocked users and users outside allowedGroups get no session. A minimal /portal page is served until W-P3-PORT-01 replaces it. Routes are mounted only when Config.Consent is set and Config.State is non-nil.

**Requirements**

- GET /portal/login stores state, nonce, the S256 PKCE verifier and `next` in oidc_pending with purpose=portal (10m TTL, single use, 10k cap), sets the `__Host-warden_portal_login` binding cookie (`warden_portal_login` on the insecure dev path), and redirects with scopes openid email profile groups, plus offline_access when idpLink is enabled. `next` accepts only a same-origin path starting with /portal/ or /connect/ (no scheme, no `//`, no backslash); anything else becomes /portal.
- GET /portal/callback consumes the pending row atomically with purpose=portal; a console state, or a missing or mismatched binding cookie, fails as state_invalid. It exchanges the code with the verifier and verifies the ID token with identity.NewIDTokenVerifier (Audience=consent clientID, AllowedAZP=[clientID], nonce, RS256/ES256, 60s skew). The identity key is (iss, sub).
- Admission: no session when BlockStore.IsBlocked(sub, email) is true (login_error=blocked), or when allowedGroups is set and no group matches (login_error=not_allowed). Groups are capped at 256.
- Migration `portal_sessions/0001` via webauth.SessionStore: portal_sessions(id_hash PK, iss, sub, email, groups_json, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at) with indexes on sub and expires_at. PortalSessionStore exposes Create, Lookup, Touch, Delete, DeleteBySub, DeleteByEmail, List and SweepExpired. Every login issues a fresh 32-byte id. Idle and absolute expiry use the CP clock.
- Cookie `__Host-warden_portal` (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, no Domain) when redirectURL is https; `warden_portal` only for http loopback or allowInsecureIssuer, with a startup warning. Secure is never derived from r.TLS.
- While discovery has not succeeded, /portal/login and /portal/callback return 503 idp_unavailable; CP start and worker routes are unaffected. Errors redirect to /portal?login_error=<code> with code from {state_invalid, nonce_mismatch, token_invalid, exchange_failed, idp_error, blocked, not_allowed, idp_unavailable}; IdP error text is never echoed.
- Each attempt logs `msg=portal_login result reason sub duration_ms` and records a login entry through the W-P1-AAUD-02 Recorder. The code, state, verifier, nonce, tokens and cookie are never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/portal/store.go (new): PortalSessionStore built with webauth.NewSessionStore(db, webauth.SessionTable{Name: "portal_sessions", MigrationID: "portal_sessions/0001"}), plus a DeleteByEmail passthrough.
2. Create internal/portal/portal.go (new): New(cfg *config.ConsentConfig, db *cpstate.DB, store secrets.SecretStore, blocks Blocklist, rec Recorder, logger) *Portal, where Blocklist is a small interface {IsBlocked(sub, email string) bool} met by controlplane.BlockStore. It holds a webauth.Flow with Purpose "portal", LoginCookie "warden_portal_login" and the next-path rule, and has Routes(mux) and Start(ctx).
3. Add handleLogin and handleCallback in internal/portal/login.go (new) on top of webauth.Flow.Begin and Flow.Complete, then the admission checks and PortalSessionStore.Create.
4. Serve a minimal no-store GET /portal stub (signed-in email, link status, logout form), replaced by W-P3-PORT-01.
5. In Server.Handler (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go) mount p.Routes only when s.cfg.Consent != nil and s.cfg.State != nil; start discovery and the sweepers from Server.Start through Portal.Start.
6. Tests in internal/portal/login_test.go (new) with webauthtest.FakeOIDC and a fake clock.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given the fake OIDC provider, when a client follows /portal/login?next=/portal/connect/abc, the provider redirect and /portal/callback, then a portal_sessions row exists for (iss, sub), Set-Cookie is __Host-warden_portal with Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, and the response redirects to /portal/connect/abc: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalLoginEndToEnd`
- [ ] A replayed state, an unknown state, a state created by /auth/login (purpose console), a missing binding cookie, a mismatched nonce, an ID token with aud=[warden-console] only, or alg HS256 each produce no portal_sessions row: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalCallbackRejects`
- [ ] Given next=https://evil.example, //evil.example or /dashboard/, the post-login redirect goes to /portal: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalNextRedirect`
- [ ] With a fake clock, a session idle for 30m01s fails to authenticate, and a session kept active fails after 8h01m: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalSessionExpiry`
- [ ] A blocked sub, a blocked email, and a user outside a non-empty allowedGroups each get no session and the matching login_error: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalAdmission`
- [ ] With the fake provider down, /portal/login returns 503 idp_unavailable while /policy answers as before; without a consent block /portal/login returns 404; captured logs hold no code, verifier, nonce, raw ID token or raw session id: `go test ./internal/portal ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPortalIdPDown|TestPortalNotMounted'`

### 3/7 · W-P3-CSIG-03

**Store the IdP refresh token in a CP-only secret namespace on login**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#130](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/130)

When consent.idpLink is enabled, the portal callback stores the user's refresh token in the CP-only consent.store (W-P3-CSIG-06) under `idp/<userKey>` and records only a Reference in idp_links. No worker holds a credential for that store, and the write is fail-closed: no token or no successful Put means no session. The table carries the generation, issue time and relink deadline that p3-offboarding needs to rotate safely and to tell Dex absolute expiry apart from a disabled user (carried forward from p1-dex).

**Requirements**

- Build the key only with secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) and secrets.IdPLinkKey(userKey) from W-P3-CSIG-06; with the default namePrefix the AWS name is `warden-cp/idp/<userKey>`.
- Startup: with consent.enabled and idpLink.enabled, the CP refuses to start unless consent.store (controlplane.NewUserStore, W-P3-CSIG-06) is configured and implements secrets.Persistent with Persists() true. An echo store is refused, and the error names the backend.
- In the callback, before creating the session: if the token response has no refresh_token, return a 502 page with code offline_access_not_granted, create no session and write nothing.
- Migration `idp_links/0001`: idp_links(iss, sub, user_key, email, secret_key, refresh_ref, generation INTEGER, linked_at, refresh_issued_at, relink_due_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status, offboarded_at, PRIMARY KEY(iss, sub)), with a unique index on user_key. No column holds a token value; refresh_ref = secrets.Ref(token).String().
- Export LinkStore{Get, List, Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, expectedGeneration, token)} for W-P3-OFFB-02. Rotate takes the per-user_key mutex, returns ErrStaleGeneration without any Put when the stored generation differs, and otherwise does the Put and then UPDATE ... WHERE generation=?, incrementing generation. Rotation does not change refresh_issued_at or relink_due_at, because Dex keeps the chain's absolute lifetime.
- Export LinkStore{Get, List, Rotate(ctx, iss, sub, expectedGeneration, token)} for W-P3-OFFB-02. Rotate does Put and then UPDATE ... WHERE generation=?, and returns ErrStaleGeneration on a mismatch. Rotation does not change refresh_issued_at or relink_due_at, because Dex keeps the chain's absolute lifetime.
- Logout and session expiry never delete the stored token. Log `msg=idp_link_stored ref generation` and record `user.idp_linked` through the W-P1-AAUD-02 Recorder; never the token.

**Implementation plan**

1. Use secrets.UserKey and secrets.IdPLinkKey from W-P3-CSIG-06; no key is built here.
2. Create internal/portal/links.go (new): the idp_links migration, LinkStore with Upsert, Get, List and Rotate, ErrStaleGeneration, and a keyed mutex.
3. In resolveConsent (cmd/proxy/controlplane.go) add the persistent-store check, using the store returned by controlplane.NewUserStore (W-P3-CSIG-06).
4. In handleCallback (internal/portal/login.go) read token.RefreshToken from the oauth2 exchange; when idpLink is enabled, run the Put and Upsert before PortalSessionStore.Create.
5. Add `link` (status, generation, relinkDueAt) to the GET /portal stub so the user sees when to sign in again.
6. Use fakes.MemorySecretStore from W-P3-CSIG-06 as consent.store in tests.
7. Tests in internal/portal/links_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given fakes.MemorySecretStore, when login completes, then the store holds `idp/<UserKey(iss,sub)>` with the provider's refresh token, and idp_links.refresh_ref equals secrets.Ref(token).String(): `go test ./internal/portal -run TestIdPLinkStored`
- [ ] With consent.store on the AWS fake and the default prefix, login writes `warden-cp/idp/<userKey>` and nothing under the distributed secretStore prefix: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestIdPLinkKeyName`
- [ ] A reflect test fails if the idp_links row type gains a field able to hold a token value: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestIdPLinksValueFree`
- [ ] A token response without refresh_token returns 502 naming offline_access, and a Put error returns 503; in both cases portal_sessions, idp_links and the store are unchanged: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestIdPLinkFailClosed`
- [ ] A second login increments generation; Rotate with a stale generation returns ErrStaleGeneration, makes no Put and leaves the stored token unchanged: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestIdPLinkRotateCAS`
- [ ] The CP refuses to start with consent and idpLink enabled and no consent.store or an echo one: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestResolveConsentRequiresPersistentStore`. Captured logs from all these tests contain no refresh token, only its Reference.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-CSIG-02`](consent-auth.md#27--w-p3-csig-02) Implement portal login, callback and session store; [`W-P3-CSIG-06`](consent-auth.md#67--w-p3-csig-06) Add the CP-only user credential store, user key helpers and reserved secret prefixes

### 4/7 · W-P3-CSIG-04

**Add the portal session middleware, CSRF, logout and console isolation**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#131](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/131)

Add the exported portal.RequireSession middleware and portal.PrincipalFrom, which later features (/connect/*, the portal page, grants) build on. Add CSRF with the console's `X-Warden-CSRF` header name (carried forward) and a portal-specific HMAC label, an Origin check, GET /portal/api/me and POST /portal/logout. Prove in tests that a portal session opens no console route and a console credential opens no portal route. Let admins list and revoke portal sessions, and end them when a user is blocked.

**Requirements**

- RequireSession reads only the portal cookie, looks the session up (idle and absolute expiry), touches last_seen_at at most once a minute, rechecks BlockStore.IsBlocked from the in-memory snapshot (a blocked principal gets 403 {"error":"user_blocked"} and its portal sessions are deleted), and puts portal.Principal{Iss, Sub, Email, Groups} in its own context key. Unauthenticated browser GETs get a 302 to /portal/login?next=<path>; API calls get 401. It ignores Authorization headers and console cookies.
- CSRF on every non-GET, HEAD or OPTIONS request behind RequireSession (/portal/*, /connect/*): the `X-Warden-CSRF` header, or a `csrf` form field on application/x-www-form-urlencoded posts, must equal HMAC-SHA256(raw session id, "warden-portal-csrf") in constant time. Origin, when present, must equal the redirectURL origin. Failures return 403 {"error":"csrf"}.
- GET /portal/api/me returns {sub, email, expiresAt, csrf, link:{status, relinkDueAt}} with Cache-Control: no-store, or 401. W-P3-PORT-01 extends this route rather than adding its own. POST /portal/logout (CSRF checked) deletes the row and clears the cookie, and keeps idp_links and the stored token.
- Isolation: the console withSession and authz table never read the portal cookie, so /dashboard/*, /central/secrets and /auth/me return 401 for a portal-only request. Worker routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest) never touch the portal store.
- Revocation: BlockStore.Add (W-P1-BLOCK-07) also calls PortalSessionStore.DeleteBySub and DeleteByEmail. GET and DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions accept ?kind=portal (admin only, W-P1-SSO-08) and return the same value-free fields.
- Logs: portal_logout, portal_csrf_denied and portal_session_revoked{by_sub, target_sub, count}, with no token, cookie or full handle. With consent disabled, all /portal/* paths return 404.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/portal/middleware.go (new): RequireSession, Principal, PrincipalFrom and the CSRF and Origin check, using webauth.CSRFToken(rawID, "warden-portal-csrf") from W-P3-CSIG-05.
2. Create internal/portal/api.go (new): handleMe and handleLogout, wired in Portal.Routes behind RequireSession.
3. In internal/controlplane/blockedusers.go (W-P1-BLOCK-03), call the portal store's DeleteBySub and DeleteByEmail from BlockStore.Add when consent is enabled.
4. In internal/controlplane/sessions_admin.go (W-P1-SSO-08), add the kind=portal branch over PortalSessionStore.List and Delete.
5. Tests in internal/portal/middleware_test.go (new) and internal/controlplane/portal_isolation_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a valid portal session, a POST behind RequireSession with no X-Warden-CSRF, a wrong value, a console-derived token or a foreign Origin returns 403, and a urlencoded post with the right `csrf` field returns 2xx: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalCSRF`
- [ ] Given only a portal cookie, GET /dashboard/api/policy, POST /central/secrets and GET /auth/me return 401. Given only a console admin session, the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN bearer, or a portal session id pasted into the console cookie name, GET /portal/api/me returns 401: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPortalConsoleIsolation`
- [ ] After POST /portal/logout, the old cookie gets 401 on /portal/api/me, and idp_links and the stored token remain: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalLogout`
- [ ] An unauthenticated browser GET /portal/connect/abc gets a 302 to /portal/login?next=%2Fportal%2Fconnect%2Fabc: `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPortalRedirectToLogin`
- [ ] Blocking a signed-in user's sub makes their next portal request 401, and an admin DELETE /dashboard/api/sessions?kind=portal&sub=<sub> does the same: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPortalSessionRevocation`
- [ ] A request to /policy carrying a portal cookie makes no call to the portal store (counted with a fake): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPortalNotOnWorkerRoutes`

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-CSIG-02`](consent-auth.md#27--w-p3-csig-02) Implement portal login, callback and session store; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#58--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route; [`W-P1-SSO-08`](console-sso-rbac.md#88--w-p1-sso-08) Add admin session list and revoke API; [`W-P1-BLOCK-07`](user-block-list.md#710--w-p1-block-07) Deny console login and sessions for blocked principals

### 5/7 · W-P3-CSIG-05

**Extract the console OIDC flow and session store into internal/webauth**

Type **chore** · Size **M** · Issue [#276](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/276)

P1 puts the OIDC login flow, the oidc_pending store, SessionStore and the session middleware inside internal/controlplane. internal/portal and internal/oauthbroker are mounted by controlplane, so they cannot import that code without an import cycle. Move the reusable parts into a new package internal/webauth, with no change to console behaviour, and add a `purpose` column so console and portal login states can never be swapped. The console tests from W-P1-SSO-03 and W-P1-SSO-04 must pass unchanged.

**Requirements**

- New package internal/webauth: Provider (lazy discovery with backoff, oauth2.Config), PendingStore over the existing oidc_pending table, Flow{Provider, Verifier, Pending, Purpose, LoginCookie, AllowNext func(string) bool} with Begin(w, r, next) and Complete(w, r) (Claims, next, error), SessionStore parameterized by SessionTable{Name, MigrationID}, a cookie helper that picks the __Host- name and flags from the redirectURL, and CSRFToken(rawID []byte, label string) string.
- Migration `oidc_pending/0002` adds `purpose TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'console'`. PendingStore.Take(stateHash, purpose) consumes the row with DELETE ... RETURNING only when the purpose matches.
- internal/controlplane/auth.go, oidc_pending.go, session.go and session_mw.go become thin wrappers over webauth. The route names, cookie names (`__Host-warden_console`, `__Host-warden_login`), the CSRF label "warden-csrf", the error codes and the log fields are unchanged.
- Move the httptest fake OIDC provider from internal/controlplane/auth_test.go to internal/webauth/webauthtest (new) as FakeOIDC, with discovery, JWKS, a token endpoint that can include or omit refresh_token, configurable aud and alg, and an on/off switch for the IdP-down tests.
- No dependency from internal/webauth on internal/controlplane, internal/dashboard or internal/portal. No new go.mod dependency.
- No secret, code, verifier, nonce, token or cookie value is logged by the moved code.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/webauth/provider.go, pending.go, flow.go, session.go, cookie.go and csrf.go (all new) by moving code from internal/controlplane/auth.go, oidc_pending.go, session.go and session_mw.go.
2. Add the oidc_pending/0002 migration and the purpose argument; the console passes "console".
3. Reduce the controlplane files to wrappers that build a webauth.Flow and webauth.SessionStore with the console's table, cookie names and label.
4. Create internal/webauth/webauthtest/fakeoidc.go (new) and point internal/controlplane/auth_test.go at it.
5. Add internal/webauth/flow_test.go and session_test.go (new) covering purpose mismatch, table parameterization and the CSRF label.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Console tests from W-P1-SSO-03, W-P1-SSO-04 and W-P1-SSO-05 pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/controlplane`
- [ ] A pending row created with purpose console is not consumed by Take(stateHash, "portal") and stays usable for the console: `go test ./internal/webauth -run TestPendingPurpose`
- [ ] Two SessionStores on different tables in the same cpstate DB do not see each other's rows, and CSRFToken differs for the same id under different labels: `go test ./internal/webauth -run 'TestSessionTables|TestCSRFLabel'`
- [ ] `go list -deps ./internal/webauth | grep -E 'internal/(controlplane|dashboard|portal)$'` prints nothing.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-03`](console-sso-rbac.md#38--w-p1-sso-03) Implement OIDC login and callback with PKCE on the control plane; [`W-P1-SSO-04`](console-sso-rbac.md#48--w-p1-sso-04) Add server-side sessions, logout, /auth/me and CSRF

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-CSIG-02`](consent-auth.md#27--w-p3-csig-02) Implement portal login, callback and session store

### 6/7 · W-P3-CSIG-06

**Add the CP-only user credential store, user key helpers and reserved secret prefixes**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#277](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/277)

Every P3 feature stores per-user credentials: IdP refresh tokens (this feature), provider grants and parked revokes (p3-oauth-broker, p3-consent-portal) and OAuth client secrets. Today the CP sends its secretStore credential to workers over SettingsWire.Secrets (internal/config/settings.go), so anything written there is readable by every worker; storeFetcher also uses a placeholder name directly as a store key, and /central/secrets can write or delete any key. Add one CP-only store, `consent.store`, that no worker ever gets a credential for, one helper that turns (iss, sub) into a fixed-length user key, and reserved logical prefixes that no static mapping or console edit can touch. This is library and config work only; nothing writes to the store until W-P3-CSIG-03 and W-P3-BRKR-04.

**Requirements**

- New internal/secrets/userkey.go: `UserKey(iss, sub string) (string, error)` returns the lowercase hex of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256("warden-user-v1\x00" + iss + "\x00" + sub), 32 characters, and errors on an empty iss or sub or one containing NUL. Key builders take that userKey: `UserGrantKey(userKey, provider)` = `users/<userKey>/<provider>`, `IdPLinkKey(userKey)` = `idp/<userKey>`, `RevokingKey(userKey, provider)` = `revoking/<userKey>/<provider>`, `UserPrefix(userKey)` = `users/<userKey>/` and `ClientSecretKey(provider)` = `oauth-clients/<provider>`. They reject a userKey that is not 32 lowercase hex characters and a provider that fails `ValidProviderID` (`^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`). No other P3 code builds these keys from raw subs.
- Reserved prefixes: `IsReservedKey(key)` is true for keys under `users/`, `idp/`, `revoking/` and `oauth-clients/`. Config validation (YAML parse, parseRemotePolicy and the CP settings and policy writers) rejects a static SecretMapping placeholder under a reserved prefix with `invalid_secret_key: reserved namespace`; storeFetcher.Fetch returns an error for reserved keys without calling Get; /central/secrets putSecret and handleSecretByKey return 403 {"error":"reserved_key"} and listSecrets leaves them out. W-P3-BRKR-06 extends the same check to /dashboard/api/secretstore.
- New `type Persistent interface { Persists() bool }`: EchoStore returns false and awsSecretStore true (the W-P3-PUS-01 Vault store will also return true). A store that does not implement it counts as non-persistent.
- New CP-local `consent.store` block (`json:"-"`, strict keys, never on SettingsWire or /policy): backend aws|vault|echo (echo only with --dev), namePrefix (default `warden-cp/`), aws {region}, vault {addr, mount, namespace, tokenEnv (default VAULT_TOKEN)}. Credentials come only from the CP environment or role; there is no key or token field in YAML. backend vault fails validation until W-P3-PUS-02 wires the W-P3-PUS-01 store.
- New controlplane.NewUserStore(cfg) returns a secrets.SecretStore that is never exposed on /central/secrets or the dashboard secret-store tab. Startup fails, naming both keys, when consent.store has the same backend as secretStore and either namePrefix is a prefix of the other.
- Docs (docs/control-plane.md, secret store section): example IAM and Vault policies that give only the CP role access to `warden-cp/*`, and a statement that worker roles and the distributed secretStore credential must never cover it. Back-compat: existing placeholders are unaffected unless they already use a reserved prefix, which now fails validation with a clear message.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create internal/secrets/userkey.go (new) with UserKey, the key builders, ValidProviderID, IsReservedKey and the prefix constants, plus a package comment describing the layout that W-P3-CSIG-03, W-P3-BRKR-04, W-P3-PORT-02 and W-P3-OFFB-01 cite.
2. In internal/secrets/store.go add Persistent and the reserved-key check in storeFetcher.Fetch; add Persists() to EchoStore (internal/secrets/echo.go) and awsSecretStore (internal/secrets/aws_store.go).
3. In internal/config/consent.go add ConsentStore with validation and EncodeNode; in internal/config/config.go add the placeholder check to the SecretMapping validation loop.
4. Create internal/controlplane/userstore.go (new) with NewUserStore and the overlap check; add the reserved-key checks to putSecret, handleSecretByKey and listSecrets in internal/controlplane/secrets.go; build the store in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go when consent.store is set.
5. Add fakes.MemorySecretStore (new, test/fakes): a value-keeping SecretStore with Persists() true and injectable Get, Put, Delete and List errors, shared by the P3 tests.
6. Tests: internal/secrets/userkey_test.go and reserved_test.go (new), consent store cases in internal/config, internal/controlplane/userstore_test.go (new) and secrets_test.go; the IAM example in docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] UserKey("https://dex", "a/b") equals a golden 32-hex value and differs from the key for sub `a+b`, for `a/b` under another issuer and for the same bytes split differently between iss and sub; empty or NUL input errors; UserGrantKey rejects provider `_idp`, `Google` and a 33-character id: `go test ./internal/secrets -run 'TestUserKey|TestKeyBuilders'`
- [ ] A policy with placeholder `idp/x`, `users/x/y` or `oauth-clients/google` fails to parse naming the reserved namespace, and storeFetcher Fetch("users/a/b") errors without calling Get: `go test ./internal/config ./internal/secrets -run 'TestReservedSecretNamespace|TestFetcherRefusesReservedKeys'`
- [ ] POST /central/secrets with key idp/a and DELETE /central/secrets/users/a/b return 403 reserved_key, and GET /central/secrets omits reserved keys: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSecretsReservedKeys`
- [ ] secretStore {aws, namePrefix warden/} with consent.store {aws, namePrefix warden/users/} fails startup naming both keys, namePrefix `warden-cp/` starts, and EchoStore reports Persists()==false while the AWS store reports true: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/secrets -run 'TestUserStoreOverlap|TestPersistent'`
- [ ] Existing secret tests pass unchanged: `go test ./internal/secrets ./internal/controlplane ./internal/config`

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-CSIG-01`](consent-auth.md#17--w-p3-csig-01) Add the CP-local consent config block and the warden-portal Dex client

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-CSIG-03`](consent-auth.md#37--w-p3-csig-03) Store the IdP refresh token in a CP-only secret namespace on login; [`W-P3-BRKR-01`](oauth-broker.md#19--w-p3-brkr-01) Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults; [`W-P3-BRKR-06`](oauth-broker.md#69--w-p3-brkr-06) Guard reserved prefixes on the worker dashboard and load client secrets from consent.store; [`W-P3-PUS-02`](refresh-model.md#212--w-p3-pus-02) Add the CP-local perUserSecrets config block and the Vault consent.store backend; [`W-P3-PUS-06`](refresh-model.md#612--w-p3-pus-06) Add guarded grant record read and write helpers; [`W-P4-NTFY-07`](user-notify.md#710--w-p4-ntfy-07) Add verified user contacts table keyed by user_key

### 7/7 · W-P3-CSIG-07

**Add a Dex-backed portal sign-in end-to-end test**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#278](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/278)

Every other ticket here tests against the httptest fake IdP. This test proves the done-when sentence against the reference identity stack, using the seeded LDAP users from W-P1-DEX-02 and the warden-portal client, in the same way W-P1-SSO-07 does for the console. It runs behind the `integration` build tag and WARDEN_IT_DEX=1, so normal `go test ./...` is unaffected.

**Requirements**

- Lives in test/integration/portal_signin_test.go (new) with `//go:build integration`, and skips unless WARDEN_IT_DEX=1. It reuses the login helper style of W-P1-SSO-07: a cookie-jar client that submits Dex's LDAP form, with no browser.
- The CP runs with console.auth=oidc, consent.enabled with issuer http://dex:5556/dex, redirectURL https://localhost:7070/portal/callback, allowInsecureIssuer true, and a persistent consent.store (the AWS fake, never echo).
- Asserts the done-when: the session cookie, the stored `idp/<userKey>` token (which successfully refreshes at the Dex token endpoint), the value-free idp_links row, 401 on /dashboard/api/* and /central/secrets with the portal cookie, CSRF 403, and 503 on /portal/login with Dex stopped while /policy still works.
- Asserts that an ID token minted for warden-portal is rejected by the worker identity verifier (aud lacks warden).
- A second sign-in by the same user records in the test log whether Dex invalidated the previous refresh token for the warden-portal client; W-P3-CSIG-03 is correct either way because of the generation check.
- Test output and captured CP logs never contain passwords, codes, cookies, ID tokens or refresh tokens.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create test/integration/portal_signin_test.go (new) reusing helpers from test/integration/integration_test.go and the W-P1-SSO-07 login helper.
2. Start the identity stack from W-P1-DEX-02 with WARDEN_PORTAL_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET set, and the CP with the consent block and a temp --state-dir.
3. Run sign-in, storage, isolation, CSRF, IdP-down and verifier-rejection checks as subtests.
4. Document the run command in docs/control-plane.md next to the console SSO test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With the identity compose stack running, `WARDEN_IT_DEX=1 go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestPortalSignIn` passes.
- [ ] User alice signs in at /portal; GET /portal/api/me returns her sub; GET /dashboard/api/traffic with the portal cookie returns 401.
- [ ] After login the backend holds `idp/<userKey>`, and that token refreshes successfully at the Dex token endpoint.
- [ ] Without the integration tag, `go vet ./test/integration` succeeds and the file is not built.
